title: How Does Scentbird Work? Plans, Queue, and What You Get Each Month
summary: How does Scentbird work? A plain guide to the plans and prices, building your queue, what ships each month, the 8 mL vials, and how to skip, pause, or cancel.
body_markdown:
Fragrance is in an interesting place right now; we’re no longer in an era of choosing one signature scent for life. Mood-based fragrance, or “olfactory mooding” as we’ve written about in[this article on Gen Z fragrance trends](https://www.scentbird.com/blog/gen-z-fragrance-trends/) , is here to stay. There is the joy of discovery, sure, but also the challenge of choosing from a genuinely huge range of designer and niche fragrances.[Scentbird](https://www.scentbird.com/) is built to answer exactly that problem. Here’s how the actual mechanics work, from picking a plan to what shows up at your door.


## **The Basic Idea**


Scentbird works on a simple loop: you pick fragrances you’re curious about, add them to a personal queue, and each month, the next one on your list ships as an 8 ml travel vial, roughly 120 to 140 sprays, enough for about a month of regular wear. You always know what’s coming next, since you control the order yourself rather than being surprised by a mystery box. When you’re done with one, the next queued fragrance ships automatically, no reordering required.


## **Choosing a Plan**


Scentbird runs three plan tiers, based on how many fragrances you want each month:


- 1 scent a month: around $17.95, the standard entry point.
- 2 scents a month: $28.50, which brings the per-scent cost down to $14.25.
- 3 scents a month: $39, working out to $13 per fragrance, the best per-scent value if you like variety or are actively building a rotation.


You can switch plans at any time from your account settings, so if one scent a month starts feeling limiting, upgrading takes a couple of clicks. A small number of premium or ultra-niche fragrances carry an additional surcharge, typically $5 to $15, on top of the base plan price, rather than being locked behind a separate tier entirely.


## **Building Your Queue**


The queue is really the heart of how Scentbird works. After signing up, you can take a short[fragrance quiz](https://www.scentbird.com/smart-recommendations) —optional, but genuinely useful if you’re not sure where to start—which uses your answers to recommend scents based on notes and families you already gravitate toward. From there, you simply browse the catalog (of around 1,000 designer and niche fragrances) and add anything that catches your interest. Yes, it’s that easy.


If you don’t actively manage your queue, Scentbird will default to sending a recommended pick based on your quiz answers and past ratings, so you’re never left with an empty shipment. You can also rate fragrances after you receive them, which helps refine future recommendations over time. A tip: taking a few minutes to curate your own list generally leads to better matches than leaving it on autopilot.


## **What Actually Arrives Each Month**


Your first shipment includes a reusable, refillable atomizer case along with your first vial, everything after that ships as a standalone 8 ml vial that clicks right into the same case. It’s designed to be travel-friendly, sturdy and small enough to clear TSA’s carry-on liquid limits with plenty of room to spare.


## **Skipping, Pausing, and Canceling**


None of this locks you in. You can skip a month if nothing in your queue appeals to you, pause your subscription if you need a break, or cancel outright, all from your account settings, with no phone call or retention pitch required. If a queued fragrance goes out of stock, Scentbird will typically move to the next item in your queue, so it’s worth checking in occasionally rather than leaving it fully unattended for months at a time.


## **Is the Vial Enough, or Should You Buy the Full Bottle?**


An 8 ml vial is meant for testing and travel, not as a permanent replacement for a full bottle. If you fall for a fragrance and want more of it long-term, Scentbird also sells[full-size bottles](https://www.scentbird.com/subscription/perfumes) , often at a discount to standard retail. The real value of the subscription model isn’t necessarily that it’s cheaper per milliliter than a full bottle bought on sale, it’s that it lets you actually live with a fragrance for a month before deciding whether it’s worth committing to at full size, which a five-second sniff at a department store counter simply can’t tell you.


## **Getting Started**


Are you ready to get started? The easiest way is to take the[fragrance quiz](https://www.scentbird.com/smart-recommendations) that we mentioned earlier; it takes a few minutes and gives your queue a real starting point. From there, Scentbird’s plans are built so you can start small with one scent a month and scale up whenever a rotation makes more sense for how you actually wear fragrance.
